chapters.title: Follow one question
chapters.checkpoint: Show the real agent status. Open compose.astronomy.json and inspect query, grafana-mcp, grafana, prometheus and loki. Resume only when ready.

beats.caption: The alert is evidence, not an instruction.
beats.speech: An alert gives us a question. It does not give us permission to run commands hidden in its text. We keep the investigation inside the disposable Astronomy Shop.

beats.caption: A session chooses a branch; code uses bounded capabilities.
beats.speech: Pi calls the bound m c p j s tool. The controller chooses the filesystem root for this conversation. The agent cannot replace that root with another session’s branch.

beats.caption: Ask through the configured datasource.
beats.speech: The query worker calls the official Grafana M C P server. Grafana routes the request to Prometheus or the added Loki datasource. The returned samples, log lines, and time window become evidence.

chapters.title: From a private tree to a visible graph
chapters.checkpoint: Show one allowed write, one denied write, then inspect actual data-bearing Grafana panels through browser_execute. Empty graphs mean the handoff is incomplete.

beats.caption: Policy checks the operation and path.
beats.speech: The filesystem policy permits our scratch and dashboard directories. A write to the protected directory should fail. This is a capability boundary, not a claim that every external side effect rolls back.

beats.caption: A virtual snapshot is not a host mount.
beats.speech: The copy on write tree stores content by hash. Our dashboard first lives inside a selected snapshot. Grafana cannot read that virtual tree as an ordinary host directory.

beats.caption: Publish one selected root explicitly.
beats.speech: The publisher reads the selected file, validates it, then replaces a file in the shared volume. Grafana provisions that file. The browser must show actual plotted samples before we call the handoff complete.

chapters.title: Share the past, separate the edits
chapters.checkpoint: Use /paired-fork in Pi. Compare branch_info for both sessions, perform independent writes, then an explicit clean merge and a conflicting merge.

beats.caption: Identical roots can share immutable content.
beats.speech: Imagine two investigations starting from the same tree. Their base root names the same immutable content. Creating another reference does not require copying every file.

beats.caption: Conversation fork plus filesystem binding is custom integration.
beats.speech: Our extension pairs a new Pi conversation with a filesystem branch. A reservation journal tracks the binding. Unbound sessions fail closed. The histories remain separate, even after filesystem changes merge.

beats.caption: Merge needs a base and a conflict policy.
beats.speech: A merge compares two roots against an explicit base. Compatible text edits can combine. Conflicts remain visible. Expected head checks prevent a stale writer from quietly replacing a newer label. We do not claim instant execution or automatic ancestry.

chapters.title: Availability has boundaries
chapters.checkpoint: Check ownership and healthy baseline. Stop only a disposable voter, observe results, restore it. For quorum loss, inspect timed-out writes after recovery before retrying.

beats.caption: The stopped node is an injected event.
beats.speech: Now we change the infrastructure, not the application diagnosis. We stop one disposable voter. Watch election state and request outcomes. A successful recovery test is evidence for that test, not continuous availability under every failure.

beats.caption: A majority is needed for writes.
beats.speech: When a majority is unavailable, writes cannot be assumed to succeed. A timeout is not proof that a write never committed. After recovery, inspect the request and label state before retrying.

beats.caption: Shared objects are a separate failure domain.
beats.speech: The three voters do not make our shared object fixture highly available. Content storage, consensus metadata, and local execution status are different promises. Keep those failure boundaries separate.

chapters.title: Defend the claim you can measure
chapters.checkpoint: Robert supplies actual contribution and decision history. Reserve 39–45 for questions. Do not extend the presentation to finish a slow demo.

beats.caption: Implementation evidence is not personal intent.
beats.speech: Explain what the code does first. Use documented history when it explains a design choice. When the reason is an inference, say so. Robert supplies his actual contribution and decision history.

beats.caption: Measure before saying fast or durable.
beats.speech: A root reference can be cheap while execution still warms a tree. A stored label can survive a restart while an external action remains outside rollback. Measure the claim at the boundary that matters.

beats.caption: A useful answer ends with a concrete test.
beats.speech: If a guarantee is not verified, name the uncertainty and the next test. The goal is a defensible engineering explanation, backed by inspectable evidence.
